results.title: Squidbrake: your AI agent needs an ankle monitor
results.content:
The team

## Every step looks fine. The chain doesn't.

AI agents can now touch cloud, production and payments. Each action they take looks fine on its own, but a chain of fine actions can add up to something nobody authorized, like deleting a production database.

Squidbrake watches the whole chain and stops the step that makes the combination dangerous.

Why now

## Agents got write access. Controls did not catch up.

Nine publicly reported cases of AI agents causing damage, or coming close, replayed against the rules Squidbrake ships with. Nothing was written for the occasion, and the one it misses is shown too.

### Replays, not the original systems

Public reports rarely publish the exact commands. Where we had to reconstruct them, each case says so. [...] The real dashboard, unedited. Three agents made 88 calls on test data, with a pilot policy that lets routine build, test and read calls through: 84 ran on their own, one was blocked (`rm -rf ~/`) and three are waiting. Squidbrake 0.3.10, captured 3 Oct 2026.

`rm -rf ~/`

## Every call, matched to a line you wrote.

Policy is one YAML file in your repo. Read it, diff it, roll it back. Every decision names the rule that made it.

`default: review`
`default_reason: A person approves anything that changes something`

`command_checks:`
 `catastrophic: block`
 `irreversible: review`
 `read_only: allow`

`rules:`
 `- id: allow-reads`
 `action: allow`
 `match: { name: ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"] }`

 `- id: allow-tests`
 `action: allow`
 `match: { input_regex: '"command":\s"(pytest|npm test)' }` [...] Backed by Entrepreneur FirstOpen source, Apache-2.0

# Your AI agent needsan ankle monitor.

Give agents real access to cloud, production and payments. Squidbrake watches the whole chain of tool calls and holds the one step that would do damage, before it runs.

The check takes 9 ms at p95. Your model takes seconds to decide. The check is the cheap part.last check 4 ms

## Inside the monitor

Four parts with one job: keep every agent inside the lines you drew, and stop it the moment it crosses one.

In pilot with a consumer services company running agents in production.

Backed by

The team
